title: PRB Starvation at Slot Time via Rank Indicator Inflation: Attacking Proportional Fair Memory in the Scheduler
text: arXiv:2611.07225 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.NI PRB Starvation at Slot Time via Rank Indicator Inflation: Attacking Proportional Fair Memory in the Scheduler Authors: Ryan Barker , Julia Boone , Tolunay Seyfi , Alirez Ebrahimi , Ethan Farquhar , Brian Davis , Joseph Boccuzzi , Fatemeh Afghah Abstract : …mean honest zero-grant runs of 41--56\,ms; RR preserves equal allocation. Exact offline replay and a Monte Carlo recurrence isolate the delivered-service denominator as the causal path. Cross-field and controller ablations show a weaker, controller-dependent channel-quality trigger, while activity-gated EWMA defenses remain structurally blind. The results mo… ▽ More Proportional fair (PF) scheduling in fifth-generation (5G) New Radio (NR) ranks user equipment (UE) by instantaneous rate over an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) of delivered service. We identify a served-but-undelivered denial-of-service (DoS) attack in which rank indicator (RI) inflation induces persistent physical resource block (PRB) starvation. Unsupported spatial layers cause first-attempt delivery failure, keeping the attacker's service EWMA low; the evaluated PF allocator repeatedly grants it the full PRB pool, denying honest UEs transmission opportunities. We formalize this recurrence and evaluate it in 3,300 paired, 200 slot multi-user shards spanning rank 1 and rank 2 Sionna Ray Tracing geometries, three link adaptation controllers, PF and round robin (RR), four target identities, and five seeds. On the rank 2 geometry, selective RI inflation yields 94--95\% target capture, reduces PRB Jain fairness from 0.997 to 0.28, and produces mean honest zero-grant runs of 41--56\,ms; RR preserves equal allocation. Exact offline replay and a Monte Carlo recurrence isolate the delivered-service denominator as the causal path. Cross-field and controller ablations show a weaker, controller-dependent channel-quality trigger, while activity-gated EWMA defenses remain structurally blind. The results motivate RI-consistency checks before feedback acquires scheduling authority and slot-time PRB evidence inside the O-RAN Distributed Unit. △ Less Submitted 4 November, 2026; originally announced November 2026. Comments: 6 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables, IEEE ICEET 979-8-3195-7952-2/26

title: Full Provenance on the COSS Causal Axis: An Event-Level Closure of Causal Attribution and Confused-Deputy Exclusion
text: arXiv:2611.07164 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CR cs.DC doi 10.5281/zenodo.23102373 Full Provenance on the COSS Causal Axis: An Event-Level Closure of Causal Attribution and Confused-Deputy Exclusion Authors: Nicola Gallo Abstract : Provenance Identity Continuity (PIC) represents an authority -use event as an operation/resource behavior situated in a causal lineage, $(o,r,\ell)\in O\times R\times L$. We make the… ▽ More Provenance Identity Continuity (PIC) represents an authority -use event as an operation/resource behavior situated in a causal lineage, $(o,r,\ell)\in O\times R\times L$. We make the causal occurrence itself primitive: a represented security-relevant causal graph $(E,\to_c)$ in which each occurrence has a unique causal history, so the consistent event-lineage space is canonically isomorphic to $E$. The modeled execution has one causal partial order; distinct lineages are distinct causal histories inside it and may share a root while diverging into incomparable branches. PIC's $O\times R\times L$ is the authority -behavior projection of this space, and Causally Ordered Security-State (COSS) continuity generalizes it to an arbitrary behavior product over the same causal execution. On this semantics we prove an architecture-independent confused-deputy exclusion theorem. PIC continuation requires $C(e')\subseteq C(e)$ on every ordinary causal edge, so descendants are bounded by their ancestors; at an ordinary join, authority available on only one incoming branch cannot be resurrected, even when branches share a common root. Non-conservative combination must be an explicit authorized composition or relaxation event. With protected-effect mediation, an effect caused by request $q$ through an ordinary authority segment can exercise only authority in $C(q)$, so a confused-deputy state is contradictory. The result holds for any system whose protected request-to-effect causes are faithfully represented and whose ordinary authority transport satisfies PIC. We revisit Rajani, Garg, and Rezk: their value, control-flow, and initial-heap attacks are different witnesses of causal ancestry, so full provenance is an evidence mechanism for recovering edges of the causal graph, not the foundation of the PIC theorem. Finally we lift it to the COSS product of heterogeneous security-state coordinates. △ Less Submitted 4 November, 2026; originally announced November 2026. Comments: 19 pages

title: Beyond Proof of Possession: A Relational Theory of Authority
text: arXiv:2611.07159 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CR cs.DC doi 10.5281/zenodo.23102206 Beyond Proof of Possession: A Relational Theory of Authority Authors: Nicola Gallo Abstract : …that an executor controls an artifact (key, token, credential, or capability), but such control alone determines neither the executor's relational profile nor the causal history of an execution occurrence. We separate PoP from Proof of Relationship (PoR), the semantic property that one execution occurrence validly continues another, and from… ▽ More Proof-of-Possession (PoP) establishes that an executor controls an artifact (key, token, credential, or capability), but such control alone determines neither the executor's relational profile nor the causal history of an execution occurrence. We separate PoP from Proof of Relationship (PoR), the semantic property that one execution occurrence validly continues another, and from authorization , which is occurrence-sensitive. The foundational change is in the semantic domain of authorization : from holders and authority -bearing artifacts to execution occurrences situated in causal histories. We give authorization models an observation-based occurrence verdict and a separate transition-admissibility relation; kernel inclusion yields a partial order on observation-kernel classes. Building on Provenance Identity Continuity (PIC) and Proof-of-Continuity (PoC), we classify executors by authorization -relevant equivalence relations whose quotients form relational profile spaces, with positive predicates over profile transitions forming a distributive lattice. This adds relational attenuation to authority attenuation: along a valid causal history, $C_{i+1}\subseteq C_i$ and $ρ_{i+1}\Rightarrowρ_i$. We prove dual monotonicity, combined closure, and origin relational closure. Two occurrences of the same authenticated executor, with the same profile and possession evidence, need not be authorization -equivalent, and within a valid PIC lineage a deputy's independent authority cannot be imported outside the origin context. Finally, we prove that the executor-dependent decision factors through the relational profile and is invariant under sound mechanisms establishing it: successor-side PoP is a possible evidence mechanism, not a necessary premise of authorization . Under explicit Witness Assumptions, a boundary-witnessed checkpoint construction realizes the premises without successor-side PoP. △ Less Submitted 4 November, 2026; originally announced November 2026. Comments: 30 pages

title: CoordX Protocol: Peer to Peer Cryptographically Verified Shared Records
text:
arXiv:2611.06034 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CR cs.DC CoordX Protocol: Peer to Peer Cryptographically Verified Shared Records Authors: David Hyland-Wood , Rob Ewin Abstract : …copy, authenticates users, and decides who has permissions to act on the record. The CoordX Protocol removes the need for that central server.
  In the CoordX protocol the author of a record holds full permission over it. Permission for any other party to create, read or update the record is assigned by explicit grants and keys. An invitation only starts con… ▽ More People, companies and software agents often must work on shared records even when they do not trust each other. Today they usually give those records to a central server. The server keeps the canonical copy, authenticates users, and decides who has permissions to act on the record. The CoordX Protocol removes the need for that central server.
  In the CoordX protocol the author of a record holds full permission over it. Permission for any other party to create, read or update the record is assigned by explicit grants and keys. An invitation only starts contact between two parties. It gives no permission. Each record is a causal tree of signed entries, and each entry is immutable. Each entry names the permission that allowed it. Any party can get the proof of that permission and check it without help from anyone. Two honest parties that check the same bytes, with the same keys and local settings, always get the same answer. The content is encrypted, so the relays that may carry it in transit see only sealed bytes. To exclude a party from future content, the other parties move to new keys. The protocol does not choose a winning version, does not put entries in time order, and does not need global agreement. Applications decide what the entries mean above the level of the protocol. △ Less Submitted 4 November, 2026; originally announced November 2026. Comments: 26 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables, currently unpublished ACM Class: C.2.2; C.2.4; D.4.6

title: Information-Matched Auditing of Conversational Emotion-Shift Forecasting: A Leakage-Safe Evaluation Protocol
text: arXiv:2611.05895 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CL cs.LG Information-Matched Auditing of Conversational Emotion-Shift Forecasting: A Leakage-Safe Evaluation Protocol Authors: Bin Wen , Dai-Qiao Zhang , Tien-Ping Tan Abstract : …information enters the representation. We present an information-matched, leakage-safe auditing protocol that closes these gaps with an explicit commitment point, executable causality tests, equal four-configuration validation searches, and seed-dialogue-aware inference. Applying it to six… ▽ More Comparisons in conversational emotion-shift forecasting are easily distorted when a learned model receives rich features but its transition baseline is given a noisy or unavailable current-emotion label, when hyperparameter budgets differ, or when target-turn information enters the representation. We present an information-matched, leakage-safe auditing protocol that closes these gaps with an explicit commitment point, executable causality tests, equal four-configuration validation searches, and seed-dialogue-aware inference. Applying it to six causal model families on four text corpora and two feature-source sensitivity configurations shows that a deployable train-only current-emotion classifier feeding the transition baseline yields a different verdict than an oracle diagnostic where both sides receive gold current emotion. Under the deployable condition, learned models improve over the predicted-label baseline on all four primary corpora; DailyDialog gains are large and survive a 72-comparison Holm correction (best ROC-AUC gain = +0.167, adjusted p=.0144). Under matched gold information, the baseline remains competitive on IEMOCAP and stronger on MELD, while every model retains a large DailyDialog advantage. We additionally report precision-recall AUC, calibration, a strictly utterance-local feature control, same-person self-shift forecasting, and a future-access dose-response test. An eight-item leakage checklist accompanies the protocol. Code, raw seed predictions, and reporting artifacts are available from the corresponding author upon request. △ Less Submitted 3 November, 2026; originally announced November 2026.

title: Chain-of-Thought Oversight Requires Separate Evidence for Faithfulness and Monitorability
text: arXiv:2611.01620 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.AI cs.CR Chain-of-Thought Oversight Requires Separate Evidence for Faithfulness and Monitorability Authors: Sichao Li , Sai Ma , Xiyang Hu , Chudi Zhong , Tongliang Liu Abstract : …reasoning visibility (whether a trace is accessible), mechanistic faithfulness (whether a trace reflects internal computation), mechanistic localizability (whether a compact causal mechanism can be isolated), and behavioral monitorability (whether a monitor can detect the target behavior). Two complementary case studies across three open-weight reasoning mod… ▽ More A common assumption in chain-of-thought (CoT) oversight is that a visible reasoning trace makes model behavior easier to monitor. We argue that this assumption can conflate distinct properties along a chain linking a model's internal computation, reasoning artifacts, outputs, and monitor judgments. We identify four properties along this chain: reasoning visibility (whether a trace is accessible), mechanistic faithfulness (whether a trace reflects internal computation), mechanistic localizability (whether a compact causal mechanism can be isolated), and behavioral monitorability (whether a monitor can detect the target behavior). Two complementary case studies across three open-weight reasoning models show why these distinctions matter. In the security vulnerability reasoning study, probes and activation ablations provide evidence of internal representation and causal influence, but a monitor with access to the reference answer does not outperform the majority-class baseline in a held-out test. In authority -hint factual reasoning study, a monitor correctly distinguishes changed from unchanged answers, but seven mechanistic analyses do not isolate a compact causal mechanism. These results show that evidence for one claim does not establish the others. We therefore propose an evidential-chain reporting standard. Each claim carries a licensing statement that specifies its target property, access tier, and artifact, and labels each required link as supported, unsupported, or assumed. These assessments determine whether the conclusion is licensed, conditionally licensed, or not licensed. △ Less Submitted 1 November, 2026; originally announced November 2026. Comments: The paper is accepted by Neurips 2026 Position Track

title: Synergetic Autonomous Intelligence: Three Axioms for Recursive Semi-Closed Learning
text: arXiv:2611.01070 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.LG Synergetic Autonomous Intelligence: Three Axioms for Recursive Semi-Closed Learning Authors: Dongxu Li Abstract : …this contract. The framework also gives finite contracts for action-effect-feedback loop re-entry, partial failure, duplicate-effect idempotency, replay, concurrent delivery, causal uncertainty, and threshold-radix state representation. KREIT, the Kernel-Ring Equilibrium Information Theory layer, treats information as a typed, resource-bounded distinction; t… ▽ More We introduce Synergetic Autonomous Intelligence (SAI), a theory and design program for learning systems that form, preserve, revise, and compose relations while continuing to learn. SAI is built on three axioms: consequential distinctions must not become orphaned (U); identity is determined by future-faithful continuation under a declared contract (I); and unresolved defects are repaired by the least lawful local completion at the lowest admitted grade (L). We model a model, agent, tool, team, or environment boundary as a recursive semi-closed system with a Kernel-Ring representation, a Compile-Open-Participate cycle, and a typed residual comparing actual with claimed continuation. Under explicit finite or affine contracts, we establish relative consistency and conditional non-redundancy of U/I/L, characterize a contract-relative semantic quotient, construct an exact joint stochastic refinement, derive a constrained residual contraction, prove finite-horizon continued-service viability, and give an executed-intervention identification result with an observational-confounding boundary. We define GRC-Close as the generative and repair schema for this contract. The framework also gives finite contracts for action-effect-feedback loop re-entry, partial failure, duplicate-effect idempotency, replay, concurrent delivery, causal uncertainty, and threshold-radix state representation. KREIT, the Kernel-Ring Equilibrium Information Theory layer, treats information as a typed, resource-bounded distinction; the control layer authorizes , executes, audits, and updates actions across cloud-edge-end scales. These results establish a common contract-level vocabulary for representation, relation, memory, action, communication, explanation, coordination, and growth, while marking the assumptions and open boundaries required for later generalization. △ Less Submitted 31 October, 2026; originally announced November 2026.

title: Circuit Oracle: Automating Attribution Graph Analysis via Natural-Language Queries
text: arXiv:2611.00420 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CL Circuit Oracle: Automating Attribution Graph Analysis via Natural-Language Queries Authors: Shariar Kabir , Hong Kiat Tan , Swastik Agrawal , Sai V R Chereddy , Sriram Balasubramanian Abstract : Attribution graphs, an emerging tool in mechanistic interpretability, use transcoders to decompose language model computations into sparse interpretable features connected by causal edges. However, turning a graph into a safety-relevant insight requires hours of manual analysis by experts. We introduce Circuit Oracle, an off-the-shelf LLM equipped with a mul… ▽ More Attribution graphs, an emerging tool in mechanistic interpretability, use transcoders to decompose language model computations into sparse interpretable features connected by causal edges. However, turning a graph into a safety-relevant insight requires hours of manual analysis by experts. We introduce Circuit Oracle, an off-the-shelf LLM equipped with a multi-agent harness and task-specific authored skills, which answers natural-language questions about a target model by reading the attribution graph through tool calls. We evaluate it on three safety-relevant proxy tasks: detecting spurious features in probe circuits, eliciting hidden knowledge from taboo-finetuned models, and suppression jailbreaking via feature-level interventions. Beyond task scores, the oracle produces pruned subgraphs and context-specific feature explanations that we assess qualitatively. Results are mixed. On spurious-feature detection, Circuit Oracle reaches 78.2 $\pm$ 2.4% accuracy, outperforming single-layer feature-ranking baselines. On secret elicitation, trained self-explainers like Activation Oracles remain the stronger baseline. On refusal suppression over 50 prompts, its single committed intervention is slightly below a diff-in-means baseline, and only exceeds it when allowed the best of five attempts. Results are stable across five runs and across model choices for the agents. We also release the pruned subgraphs and context-specific feature readings that revise existing global labels, and invite future work to develop evaluations that can measure their usefulness directly. △ Less Submitted 30 October, 2026; originally announced November 2026. Comments: Extended version of a paper presented at the Mechanistic Interpretability and Compositional Learning workshops at ICML 2026

title: The Knowledge Layer Model (KLM): Evidence-Visible AI Output, Routing Diagnostics, and Negative Results
text: arXiv:2610.42066 [ pdf ] cs.AI cs.CL The Knowledge Layer Model (KLM): Evidence-Visible AI Output, Routing Diagnostics, and Negative Results Authors: Omer Asim Ozturk , Cihan Aydiner Abstract : …disclosure was not accepted. Restoration, re-derivation, human-rubric support, boundary isolation, and bounded-response evaluations remain proposed. Findings are internal and author -reported; historical observations are distinguished from later reproductions. Evidence visibility does not establish correctness, causal r… ▽ More AI answers require more than apparent correctness: reviewers need to inspect their recorded basis. We introduce the Knowledge Layer Model (KLM), an open, implementation-neutral specification for inference records with versioned epistemic assessments, evidence relations, and explicit unknowns. SEDIM, the knowledge and evidence architecture of Nage AI OS, is a reference implementation. We reference KLM v0.3 (repository tag v0.3.0). Empirical material consists of separate internal experiments, not end-to-end validation. A historical platform-domain routing benchmark reports 137/150 classifications across 15 classes (91.3%; nominal 95% Wilson interval 85.7-94.9%); the numerator is recovered from a rounded summary, and historical example membership is unverified. A native-model weight-path configuration yielded 0/15 successful answers in a corrected two-source test. A capacity-growth comparison could not establish a reliable effect because of a defective legacy scorer and missing original outputs. Lexical and scoped diagnostics each yielded AUC 0.008 for silent-versus-contradicted examples, below the registered minimum of 0.65. Legacy packing lost gold-containing text in 118/221 selected cases; repaired packing retained it in 221/221. These measure text presence, not answer quality. Python and TypeScript verifiers reportedly agreed on six checks per synthetic fixture; a separate production disclosure was not accepted. Restoration, re-derivation, human-rubric support, boundary isolation, and bounded-response evaluations remain proposed. Findings are internal and author -reported; historical observations are distinguished from later reproductions. Evidence visibility does not establish correctness, causal reliance, security, or regulatory compliance. Independent replication and a complete public audit package remain future work. △ Less Submitted 30 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026. Comments: 47 pages, 1 figure, 14 tables. Includes Appendix A

title: Adversarial Process Disturbances at a Deployable Alarm Budget: Detector Evaluation on a Simulator and a Real Plant
text: arXiv:2610.38786 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CR Adversarial Process Disturbances at a Deployable Alarm Budget: Detector Evaluation on a Simulator and a Real Plant Authors: Benjamin Blakely Abstract : …large drops, with unstable rankings, on real plant data. We ask whether that extends to the security case. We evaluate eleven detectors across classical, neural, dependency and causal families on a simulated chemical process and a sodium thermal-hydraulic facility: different processes sharing no equipment, but both continuous, at steady state, and perturbed… ▽ More Industrial anomaly detection is evaluated largely on simulators, and recent work reports large drops, with unstable rankings, on real plant data. We ask whether that extends to the security case. We evaluate eleven detectors across classical, neural, dependency and causal families on a simulated chemical process and a sodium thermal-hydraulic facility: different processes sharing no equipment, but both continuous, at steady state, and perturbed only through temperature, pressure, flow and valve, never composition. Three conditions prior work does not cover: disturbances authored against a threat model rather than native faults; one construction applied to both processes; and detection read at a declared false-alarm budget. The drop persists throughout. The simulator panel looks deployable, neural matching classical; on plant telemetry detection collapses and the neural family trails, a gap that in-sample thresholds likely understate. Which detector wins transfers between the two processes; how often it fires does not. Two results hold on both. Sequential valve manipulation defeats the whole panel: at tier 2 no detector flags more than 0.17 of its perturbed samples, against 0.89 or better for most disturbances. And the plant's collapse is not merely that its disturbances are weaker, though they are by about twelvefold; matched on measured strength, the plant is never the better detected. △ Less Submitted 28 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026.

title: Alpha-TCM: A Nine-Layer Framework for TCM-Guided Multimodal Inference and Structured-Prior Auditing
text:
arXiv:2610.38754 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.LG Alpha-TCM: A Nine-Layer Framework for TCM-Guided Multimodal Inference and Structured-Prior Auditing Authors: Yucheng Liu , Everett X. Wang Abstract : Alpha-TCM makes two contributions under a central thesis: auditable systems should separate domain knowledge, case evidence, probabilistic inference, and downstream authority . First, it proposes a nine-layer TCM-oriented architecture covering semantic definitions, multimodal acquisition, quality control, provenance-bearing knowledge, probabilistic inference,… ▽ More Alpha-TCM makes two contributions under a central thesis: auditable systems should separate domain knowledge, case evidence, probabilistic inference, and downstream authority . First, it proposes a nine-layer TCM-oriented architecture covering semantic definitions, multimodal acquisition, quality control, provenance-bearing knowledge, probabilistic inference, longitudinal updating, constrained decisions, language interaction, and human governance. Each layer specifies its information contract, failure boundary, dependencies, and validation status. This is a system-design proposal, not a claim of complete clinical implementation.
  Second, a controlled synthetic prototype instantiates Layers 1-5 to audit the knowledge-evidence interface. Four conditional-Gaussian encoders process synthetic tongue images, pulse waveforms, inquiry fields, and text, while a frozen bridge predicts a five-dimensional synthetic outcome. A versioned contextual prior is compiled independently of the renderer. Fusion removes duplicated reference-prior information before adding context. Equal-information controls, prior regularization, graded contamination, and structural corruption test contextual benefits, Bayesian specificity, and conflict detection.
  Across ten paired seeds and four training sizes, contextual knowledge improved mean absolute error over marginal committee fusion at 600 and 1,200 cases, but not over equal-information neural controls. Fully incorrect context harmed performance at every size, while prior effects were inconsistent and conflict scores did not track case-level damage. The results support contextual structure in low-data synthetic settings, not a specifically Bayesian advantage. The prototype establishes no claims about TCM theory or clinical, diagnostic, therapeutic, causal , longitudinal, or transfer validity. △ Less Submitted 28 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026.

title: From Voiceprints to User Entities: Online Speaker-Memory Construction for Multi-User Spoken Agents
text: arXiv:2610.36713 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.SD cs.AI eess.AS From Voiceprints to User Entities: Online Speaker-Memory Construction for Multi-User Spoken Agents Authors: Yucong Zhang , Cancan Li , Bo Xiao , Ke Zeng , Ming Li Abstract : …and formulate online speaker-memory construction to maintain persistent user entities as acoustic evidence evolves. We introduce EvoSpeakerMem, a training-free layer for causal speaker routing, selective acoustic-state updates, and identity-partitioned memory writes and retrieval through a replaceable text-memory backend. We also construct LoCoMo-ID, a spok… ▽ More Personalized spoken agents must identify speakers before accessing user-specific memory, yet memory benchmarks typically assume correctly attributed histories. We argue that voiceprints are observations of identity, not identities themselves, and formulate online speaker-memory construction to maintain persistent user entities as acoustic evidence evolves. We introduce EvoSpeakerMem, a training-free layer for causal speaker routing, selective acoustic-state updates, and identity-partitioned memory writes and retrieval through a replaceable text-memory backend. We also construct LoCoMo-ID, a spoken-memory benchmark with hidden speaker identities, speaker-sensitive queries, simulated recording-condition shifts, and four-speaker identity-confusion tests. On longitudinal SMIIP-TV, genuine-probe rejection under a frozen near-enrollment threshold rises from 29.8% to 55.6% over approximately one year. On LoCoMo-ID speaker-sensitive queries, gated updating improves identity-gated QA over fixed representations by 3.86 and 11.62 percentage points under clean and shifted conditions, respectively, with no wrong-user authorizations . The advantage persists in the four-speaker test. Yet reducing fragmentation and improving QA can coexist with incorrect cross-user links, revealing a fragmentation--contamination trade-off that QA alone cannot capture. △ Less Submitted 27 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026. Comments: Preprint

title: A Hybrid Framework for Explainable Aviation Risk: Causal Chain Extraction from Safety Reports with Physics-Based Failure Quantification and Interventional Analysis
text: arXiv:2610.35658 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.LG eess.SY stat.AP A Hybrid Framework for Explainable Aviation Risk: Causal Chain Extraction from Safety Reports with Physics-Based Failure Quantification and Interventional Analysis Authors: Yutian Pang , Yifang Tian , Xinyu Zhao , Jueming Hu , John-Paul Clarke , Hans-Arno Jacobsen Abstract : Aviation authorities hold decades of accident reports whose narratives record how investigators reconstructed each accident. Computational work on these archives has mostly sorted reports into fixed taxonomies. In this work, we propose a hybrid framework in which a text-based corpus identifies the leading factors of a failure mode. Physics-based models then… ▽ More Aviation authorities hold decades of accident reports whose narratives record how investigators reconstructed each accident. Computational work on these archives has mostly sorted reports into fixed taxonomies. In this work, we propose a hybrid framework in which a text-based corpus identifies the leading factors of a failure mode. Physics-based models then quantify how likely that failure is at a stated operating point. Ordered causal chains extracted from 56{,}202 American accident reports with a local large language model aggregate into a causation knowledge graph. On an evaluation sample of 2{,}000 reports, the chains recover 90.8\% of investigator-flagged causes. Each physical factor whose drivers the record carries receives an occurrence model calibrated to the accident population. A leaky noisy-OR fitted to the corpus combines the factors into a failure mode probability that supports intervention. For engine power loss, the carburetor icing model separates 1{,}205 icing accidents from other accidents using temperature and dewpoint alone, reaching 0.61 in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve against a density ratio ceiling of 0.64. Routine weather hours give no valid control, because flying concentrates in fair weather. On later years the physics adds 0.03 to that area for occurrence and nothing for severity, so its value lies in interpretability. On four named accidents, abduction gives a probability of necessity of 0.29 to 0.50 for the heat omission, under monotonicity. The Fast Causal Inference algorithm does not license the largest backdoor adjustment on the learned networks. △ Less Submitted 4 November, 2026; v1 submitted 26 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026. Comments: 14 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables. v2 prints the carburetor icing scenario values to four digits, corrects wording and table formatting, and removes one author from the author list at his request. This work is going to be submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

title: PhysEvolve: Verifier-grounded Self-evolution for Physical Reasoning with Executable Worlds
text: arXiv:2610.34921 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.AI PhysEvolve: Verifier-grounded Self-evolution for Physical Reasoning with Executable Worlds Authors: Jinyuan Hu , Yilei Jiang , Chen Tang , Minghong Cai , Xinran Liu , Xiangyu Yue Abstract : …reasoning underpins how embodied systems understand and act in the physical world, yet vision-language models (VLMs) remain unreliable on questions about dynamics and physical causality . Progress is critically constrained by the scarcity of grounded counterfactual training data, as observational videos capture only the factual trajectory that occurred. The s… ▽ More Physical reasoning underpins how embodied systems understand and act in the physical world, yet vision-language models (VLMs) remain unreliable on questions about dynamics and physical causality . Progress is critically constrained by the scarcity of grounded counterfactual training data, as observational videos capture only the factual trajectory that occurred. The self-evolving paradigm offers a route beyond fixed datasets by enabling models to construct their own training problems. Extending this paradigm to physics, however, requires an external source of truth that can both validate model-proposed environments and verify alternative physical outcomes under intervention. We introduce \physevolve{}, a verifier-grounded self-evolving framework that trains VLMs for causal physical reasoning from model-proposed executable worlds and simulation- authored tasks. At each round, a shared VLM proposes executable world programs and evidence schemas; a deterministic physics engine freezes each valid world, simulates matched baseline and body-elided counterfactual branches, and synthesizes discrete, answer-bound visual tasks. Exact verifier feedback from task solving updates both the shared policy via GRPO and an adaptive curriculum over physical intents. Starting from Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, \physevolve{} achieves targeted gains across PhysBench, CausalPhys, and ContPhy without human intervention data, improving PhysBench Throwing by $8.8$ points and ContPhy Counterfactual Removal and Goal-Pit by $7.4$ and $24.4$ points. These gains concentrate on interaction-sensitive and altered-world questions, demonstrating zero-shot transfer of causal principles to unseen complex dynamics (cloth, fluid, soft bodies) and real-world video. △ Less Submitted 26 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026. Comments: Preprint

title: Causal Humility: Governing the Authority of Fairness Claims Under Causal Uncertainty
text:
arXiv:2610.25709 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CY cs.AI Causal Humility: Governing the Authority of Fairness Claims Under Causal Uncertainty Authors: Khadija Zanna , Rodrigo Ferreira , Frederick L. Oswald , Akane Sano Abstract : …for auditing and governance. Fairness assessment often requires more than identifying disparities in outcomes; it also requires understanding how those disparities arise. Causal approaches to algorithmic fairness address this explanatory problem by representing pathways through which protected attributes and other factors may influence outcomes. Yet… ▽ More AI systems increasingly shape consequential decisions in employment, lending, healthcare, and public services, making fairness an important problem for auditing and governance. Fairness assessment often requires more than identifying disparities in outcomes; it also requires understanding how those disparities arise. Causal approaches to algorithmic fairness address this explanatory problem by representing pathways through which protected attributes and other factors may influence outcomes. Yet causal reasoning in sociotechnical systems remains uncertain: relevant confounders may be unobserved, causal directions contested, and conclusions sensitive to modeling assumptions and representational choices.
  We introduce causal humility as a governance framework for managing the relationship between epistemic uncertainty and causal authority . Drawing on causal fairness research, epistemology, political philosophy, and science and technology studies, causal humility has four requirements: making consequential assumptions and omissions visible; preserving contestability across defensible causal accounts; recognizing indeterminacy as a legitimate analytical outcome; and maintaining proportionality between evidentiary support and institutional authority or action.
  We operationalize these requirements through Causal Cards, a documentation artifact for recording the causal basis, assumptions, omissions, model dependence, and governance implications of fairness claims. Using the UCI Adult dataset as a worked epistemic demonstration, we show how different causal discovery procedures applied to the same observational data render fairness-relevant pathways visible, absent, or unresolved. Causal humility treats such disagreement as information about the limits of what can responsibly be claimed and the authority those claims should carry. △ Less Submitted 18 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026.

title: Memory, Know Your PLACE: Governing Lifecycle State and Query-Time Eligibility in Persistent-Memory Agents
text: arXiv:2610.25179 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.AI cs.CL Memory, Know Your PLACE: Governing Lifecycle State and Query-Time Eligibility in Persistent-Memory Agents Authors: Chen-Fang Hu , Hong-Han Shuai , Woan-Shiuan Chien Abstract : …governance over both state formation and query-time influence. We introduce PLACE, a factorized governance layer that adds write-side state certification and read-side authorization to a memory backend. A factorial evaluation on Mem0 with Qwen2.5-3B and Qwen2.5-7B isolates the contribution of each mechanism. Results show that write-side governance substantia… ▽ More Persistent memory turns prior interactions into durable agent state, but existing systems provide limited control over whether that state remains valid and whether it should influence a later query. We argue that reliable memory requires governance over both state formation and query-time influence. We introduce PLACE, a factorized governance layer that adds write-side state certification and read-side authorization to a memory backend. A factorial evaluation on Mem0 with Qwen2.5-3B and Qwen2.5-7B isolates the contribution of each mechanism. Results show that write-side governance substantially improves lifecycle state correctness, while read-side governance eliminates measured causal leakage from ineligible memory in the state-correct setting. Their combination achieves the strongest joint performance while preserving query-relevant support. These findings show that reliable persistent memory requires explicit control over both maintained state and query-time information influence. △ Less Submitted 18 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026.

title: Learning When to Withdraw: Curriculum Coverage and Rule-Specific Failures in Fine-Tuned Language Agents
text: arXiv:2610.21045 [ pdf ] cs.AI Learning When to Withdraw: Curriculum Coverage and Rule-Specific Failures in Fine-Tuned Language Agents Authors: Mohamed Abouzahra Abstract : Tool-using language agents must revise prepared actions when evidence changes or authority is revoked. Selective withdrawal means suspending affected actions, preserving supported work, and resuming only after sufficient repair. We study supervised fine-tuning in NAQD-Env, a synthetic environment with explicit dependencies and a deterministic reference polic… ▽ More Tool-using language agents must revise prepared actions when evidence changes or authority is revoked. Selective withdrawal means suspending affected actions, preserving supported work, and resuming only after sufficient repair. We study supervised fine-tuning in NAQD-Env, a synthetic environment with explicit dependencies and a deterministic reference policy. Four LoRA checkpoints of Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct compare an original curriculum with an enriched one, the latter under three system-prompt framings with identical views and targets. Three instruction-tuned baselines and all four checkpoints are evaluated under three inference prompts on fresh validation cases, held-out dependency families, and held-out structural combinations. Under the naqd prompt, SFT checkpoints reach decision agreement of 0.77-0.92 and withdrawal recall of 0.46-0.86, versus 0.45-0.63 and at most 0.06 for the baselines. Rule-level diagnostics qualify these gains. The original-curriculum checkpoint wrongly withdraws 26 of 34 actions with surviving alternative support; enriched checkpoints withdraw 0-1. Conversely, all SFT checkpoints narrow prohibited combinations less often than the 7B and 8B baselines, a case absent from both curricula. Delegation results show more withdrawal but poorer preservation of independently authorized actions, and all four checkpoints omit valid event reports. Framing contrasts vary across metrics and splits and do not establish a reproducible advantage or equivalence. One training run per arm, jointly changed curriculum properties, prior evaluation exposure, and baseline-SFT quantization differences limit causal attribution. The contribution is a method for detecting rule-specific regressions that aggregate accuracy can conceal, not evidence that fine-tuning alone ensures agent safety. △ Less Submitted 14 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026.

title: REPORT-OPS: Hybrid Evidence-Guided Reporting with Human-Supervised Refinement for HPC
text: arXiv:2610.19222 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.AI REPORT-OPS: Hybrid Evidence-Guided Reporting with Human-Supervised Refinement for HPC Authors: Mah Kadidia Konate , Mayur Akewar , Janki Bhimani , Steven Farrell Abstract : …Producing a reliable report requires more than retrieving relevant records: the evidence must refer to the correct system, metric definition, time period, and source of authority . We present REPORT-OPS, a hybrid reporting agent in which an LLM interprets requests, plans evidence collection, evaluates possible explanations, and drafts reports, while… ▽ More Operational reporting for high-performance computing (HPC) facilities requires combining information from monitoring services, schedulers, incident and maintenance records, storage measurements, periodic reports, and operator investigations. Producing a reliable report requires more than retrieving relevant records: the evidence must refer to the correct system, metric definition, time period, and source of authority . We present REPORT-OPS, a hybrid reporting agent in which an LLM interprets requests, plans evidence collection, evaluates possible explanations, and drafts reports, while author -seeded operational policies and automated checks determine whether the available evidence supports the requested conclusion. Depending on the evidence state, the system answers the request, reports a qualified conclusion, or withholds an unsupported claim. During offline refinement, an LLM critic proposes bounded policy changes that a human approves or rejects without editing; accepted candidates are promoted only after automated target, held-out, and regression testing. We evaluate REPORT-OPS on 68 sanitized reporting queries constructed from 50 base scenarios in a frozen HPC operational corpus, using three agent models and two LLM judges. REPORT-OPS achieves 68.63% Pass@80, compared with 7.02% for the strongest retrieval baseline. Evidence gating increases claim-support precision from 40.58% to 90.06%. On the 13-query explanatory subset, explanation accuracy reaches 55.54%. Across five rounds of human-supervised refinement, localized policy updates correct 91.17% of targeted failures and improve performance on related held-out cases by 9.33 percentage points, with no observed regression breaks under release gating. These results demonstrate improved evidence-grounded reporting and within-environment policy reuse; they do not establish unrestricted causal discovery or cross-facility generalization. △ Less Submitted 13 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026. Comments: Konate and Akewar contributed equally to this work

title: Formal-Verification-Guided Bayesian Optimization for Non-Intrusive Last-Mile Coverage Closure
text: arXiv:2610.17449 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.AR cs.LG Formal-Verification-Guided Bayesian Optimization for Non-Intrusive Last-Mile Coverage Closure Authors: Chengjia Liu , Priyadarsi Mishra , David Kebo Houngninou , Michael Quinn , Aakash Tyagi , Jiang Hu Abstract : …environment exposes many controls while direct hits on the remaining bins are sparse. We present a non-intrusive workflow that closes pre-defined bins in an existing, human- authored functional coverage model; it does not synthesize verification objectives from the design specification. The workflow first uses abstract-syntax-tree (AST) parsing and cone-of-in… ▽ More Last-mile functional coverage closure for modern chip designs remains costly because a mature UVM environment exposes many controls while direct hits on the remaining bins are sparse. We present a non-intrusive workflow that closes pre-defined bins in an existing, human- authored functional coverage model; it does not synthesize verification objectives from the design specification. The workflow first uses abstract-syntax-tree (AST) parsing and cone-of-influence (COI) tracing to map each residual target to existing testbench knobs. Under a matched 20-simulation budget, Bayesian optimization (BO) is compared with continued constrained-random verification (CRV) and random search over the same AST/COI-reduced space. Formal reachability then removes only targets supported by complete unreachability proofs, after which retained targets are grouped by formal difficulty and processed by group-specific BO under a second matched 20-simulation budget. Cleanup and grouping never add numerator bins; only simulator coverage artifacts do. On OpenTitan AES, first-pass reduced-space BO reaches 241/271 bins; formal cleanup removes two denominator bins; the integrated post-cleanup stage - difficulty grouping, policy routing, and group-specific BO - adds 20 simulator-confirmed hits, yielding 261/271 raw coverage (96.31%) and 261/269 effective coverage (97.03%). On Entropy Source, first-pass reduced-space BO reaches 2117/2277 bins; formal cleanup removes ten denominator bins; the integrated post-cleanup stage - difficulty grouping, policy routing, and group-specific BO - adds 93 simulator-confirmed hits, yielding 2210/2277 raw coverage (97.06%) and 2210/2267 effective coverage (97.49%). These results characterize the integrated diagnosis-and-search workflow; the present evaluation does not isolate the causal contributions of difficulty classification, policy routing, and post-cleanup BO. △ Less Submitted 12 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026. Comments: 21 pages, 3 figures, 7 tables. Accepted for publication in ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems (TODAES)

title: From Observations to Authorized Actions: Measuring Source Information in Android Agents
text: arXiv:2610.15502 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CR cs.OS From Observations to Authorized Actions: Measuring Source Information in Android Agents Authors: Hyobin Ahn , Dongjae Lee Abstract : Android agents read content from applications and web pages and act on it with the user's authority , yet they cannot reliably tell where that content came from -- its source, the application or document that supplied it. The WebView accessibility fields we inspected expose the host application but omit the document origins available inside the browser, s… ▽ More Android agents read content from applications and web pages and act on it with the user's authority , yet they cannot reliably tell where that content came from -- its source, the application or document that supplied it. The WebView accessibility fields we inspected expose the host application but omit the document origins available inside the browser, so an agent reading through this interface cannot check which document supplied an object; a limited reproduction on an unmodified WebView yields the same finding. We build and separately evaluate two prototypes to examine how source information supports authorization . Our application-source monitor withholds side-effecting calls whose signed source record contains an untrusted application. With the source set derived from the OS accessibility log, it blocked every selected attack write in the tested runs, but it also withheld benign sends issued after reading untrusted content, flagged benign tasks that use external content, and carried source records into a later clean task. Our WebView source-reference gate uses records from a modified browser to check object origins and reference lifetime through direct calls; in a separate 24-trial evaluation, the live agent selected no disallowed object. Supporting benchmark and planner measurements characterize textual argument matches and attacker-target selection, without establishing causal dataflow or a controlled model ranking. The prototypes are not an integrated defense: the WebView gate still lacks authenticated browser delivery and atomic capture of selected bytes and origin. Together, the results show which source information the tested policies need and why it must stay linked to the object used in execution. △ Less Submitted 11 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026. Comments: 18 pages, 2 figures

title: From Reactive Containment to Proactive Assurance: Lessons from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Agent Security Incidents
text: arXiv:2610.12463 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CR cs.AI From Reactive Containment to Proactive Assurance: Lessons from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Agent Security Incidents Authors: Abbas Raftari Abstract : In 2026, cybersecurity evaluations involving OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google agents reached real systems outside their authorized test scope. The paths were different. OpenAI agents exploited research infrastructure, coordinated across runs, and compromised parts of Hugging Face's production environment. Anthropic reported cases in which a misconfigured th… ▽ More In 2026, cybersecurity evaluations involving OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google agents reached real systems outside their authorized test scope. The paths were different. OpenAI agents exploited research infrastructure, coordinated across runs, and compromised parts of Hugging Face's production environment. Anthropic reported cases in which a misconfigured third-party environment exposed real systems to agents pursuing simulated cyber tasks. In a separately reported evaluation, Google's Gemini accessed three real organizations through an unintended internet route; Google stated that the model stopped in all three instances. Taken together, the cases show why an evaluation cannot rely on an assumed boundary. That boundary must be verified while the agent is operating. This comparative instrumental case study develops a Proactive Agent Security Assurance Cycle (PASAC) and a five-layer Boundary Assurance Stack. The framework combines risk-tiered task design, executable scope contracts, pre-run validation, least-capability access, independent egress enforcement, credential restrictions, cross-run monitoring, automatic stop conditions, and evidence-based reauthorization. A leading-indicator model, nine design propositions, and seven falsifiable hypotheses turn these lessons into a testable research program. Because the public Gemini record is limited to attributed statements and journalism, its detailed causal mechanism remains provisional. The central conclusion is straightforward: proactive agent security requires continuous assurance across the full execution system, not confidence in any single sandbox or safeguard. △ Less Submitted 8 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026. Comments: Conceptual research paper; includes one framework figure. The manuscript proposes a model-agnostic Boundary Assurance Stack for proactive security and accountable human oversight of high-capability AI agents

title: Whose Memory Is It? Scope-Aware Commit Rules for Long-Term LLM Memory
text: arXiv:2610.09008 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.AI Whose Memory Is It? Scope-Aware Commit Rules for Long-Term LLM Memory Authors: Hongyu Gu , Xinchang Li Abstract : …context as \emph{discourse ownership}: the world, branch, or speaker that licenses a proposition. Our first finding is counterintuitive. Language models already carry a causally active signal for ownership, yet conventional memory interfaces discard it when they convert reasoning into records. We introduce CASK (… ▽ More Persistent memory allows an LLM agent to carry experience across conversations, but it also turns a local reasoning mistake into a durable one. During deliberation, an agent may consider a plan, simulate a tool result, report another speaker's belief, and then reject all of them. If memory retains only the resulting sentences, those once-useful possibilities can later return as facts. The record is neither fabricated nor irrelevant; it has simply been detached from the context in which it was valid. We identify this missing context as \emph{discourse ownership}: the world, branch, or speaker that licenses a proposition. Our first finding is counterintuitive. Language models already carry a causally active signal for ownership, yet conventional memory interfaces discard it when they convert reasoning into records. We introduce CASK ( Causally Anchored Scoping Keys), a commit rule that preserves this signal so that shared-world facts enter durable memory while provisional content remains available only within its original scope. Our second finding is that the most obvious way to preserve the signal---storing the discovered internal coordinates---is unreliable because equivalent representations need not keep the same coordinates. CASK instead preserves the stable relations that express ownership. Controlled long-conversation conflicts and tool-agent traces show that this design improves memory admission and prevents provisional content from contaminating later answers while complementing runtime provenance. The resulting commit boundary lets agents explore more possibilities without granting every intermediate sentence authority over future behavior. △ Less Submitted 6 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026. Comments: 20 pages, 2 figures Journal ref: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop LP4FM Poster, https://openreview.net/forum?id=jXE0A1Pv0T

title: When the Rule-Maker Runs the World Championship: Late Patches and Procedural Accountability in League of Legends
text: arXiv:2610.07427 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CY When the Rule-Maker Runs the World Championship: Late Patches and Procedural Accountability in League of Legends Authors: Haewoon Kwak Abstract : Riot Games, which runs the League of Legends World Championship (Worlds), also changes the game shortly before each tournament. This concentration of authority raises a governance question: Who scrutinizes how the benefits and burdens of late rule changes are distributed? We examine all ten championships from 2016 to 2025, combining 1,097 games, 215 team-yea… ▽ More Riot Games, which runs the League of Legends World Championship (Worlds), also changes the game shortly before each tournament. This concentration of authority raises a governance question: Who scrutinizes how the benefits and burdens of late rule changes are distributed? We examine all ten championships from 2016 to 2025, combining 1,097 games, 215 team-years, and LLM coding of 1,090 champion changes across 40 patches. On average, 33% of a team's prior picks were on champions with net nerfs in the patches it had not played before Worlds, and 8% were on champions with net buffs. Within a year, the median gap between the most and least affected teams was 23 percentage points for nerfed picks and 12 for buffed picks. Nerfs fell mainly on the most-contested champions and buffs on less-contested ones, as Riot's published balancing criteria anticipate. Pools concentrated on the prevailing meta therefore had more negative net exposure, and even the winners of a year's four major regional leagues differed in net exposure about as much as four randomly drawn teams. Higher buff exposure was associated with additional opponent bans on buffed champions, although its size depends on the model. Among quarterfinalists, the most buff-exposed team of each year reached six of ten finals and won four titles. The team with the most negative net exposure reached two finals and won one. These exploratory descriptions identify unequal exposure, not causal gains or losses. The association between net exposure and winning remains uncertain, at +1.3 percentage points per standard deviation with a 95% interval from -0.9 to +3.7. We argue that scrutiny of late rulemaking should not depend on proving that a patch changed who won Worlds. Earlier patch commitments, team-level impact disclosure, independent review, and a formal opportunity to challenge decisions would make publisher authority more accountable. △ Less Submitted 5 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026. Comments: 29 pages, 3 figures, 11 tables ACM Class: K.4.1; K.8.0; J.4

title: PaxosLease in Relativistic Inertial Frames
text: arXiv:2610.02879 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.DC physics.class-ph PaxosLease in Relativistic Inertial Frames Authors: Márton Trencséni Abstract : A lease grants one holder exclusive authority over a resource for a fixed term, and its safety property guarantees that at most one holder has the lease at any time. Under special relativity ``at any time'' has no frame-independent meaning for participants in relative motion. This note first restates the classical safety property with light cones, re… ▽ More A lease grants one holder exclusive authority over a resource for a fixed term, and its safety property guarantees that at most one holder has the lease at any time. Under special relativity ``at any time'' has no frame-independent meaning for participants in relative motion. This note first restates the classical safety property with light cones, requiring a holder's expiry to lie in the causal past of any later acquisition by a different holder, an order every observer agrees about. Second, the paper modifies classical PaxosLease: the core change is that the containment and quarantine rules each gain a factor of $k = \sqrt{(1+β)/(1-β)}$, the relativistic Doppler factor, where $β$ is relative speed as a fraction of the speed of light. △ Less Submitted 2 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026. Comments: 6 pages, 4 figures, 1 table

title: Intrusion Detection for Agentic Processes: Evidence-Based Runtime Monitoring
text: arXiv:2610.00151 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CR Intrusion Detection for Agentic Processes: Evidence-Based Runtime Monitoring Authors: Arslan Brömme Abstract : …access, and human approval. Security-relevant deviations can therefore emerge across an evolving process rather than in one isolated input or action. Building on the author's earlier black-box architecture for agentic processes and the subsequent evidence-claim model, this paper proposes an Agentic-Process Intrusion Detection System (A-IDS), an evidence-… ▽ More Agent deployments increasingly combine language-model inference with retrieval, delegation, tool execution, external-system access, and human approval. Security-relevant deviations can therefore emerge across an evolving process rather than in one isolated input or action. Building on the author's earlier black-box architecture for agentic processes and the subsequent evidence-claim model, this paper proposes an Agentic-Process Intrusion Detection System (A-IDS), an evidence-aware security interpretation layer for runtime intrusion detection whose monitored object is the agentic process itself. A-IDS compares evidence-supported observations with a governed and versioned expectation baseline for workflow state, authorization , communication, and mandatory events. Its conceptual contribution combines dynamically due governed expectations, visibility separated from three-valued matching, explicit unresolved observation states, and bounded findings that separate evidentiary status from operational impact. The model further identifies the monitoring plane itself as an attack surface when adversarial content reaches semantic evidence producers through otherwise legitimate observation paths. Some observations may be produced outside the operational agent's self-report path, but the model does not assume complete observability or universally trustworthy capture. Prompt injection is treated both as an input-security problem and as a possible origin of later process deviations and cross-agent influence paths. A-IDS does not infer malicious intent from anomalous behavior, does not treat an unobserved event as proof of non-occurrence, and does not claim a new anomaly detector, temporal logic, or provenance model. The contribution is conceptual: it does not validate an implementation, demonstrate empirical detection performance, establish causal attribution, or provide an enforcement mechanism. △ Less Submitted 10 September, 2026; originally announced October 2026. Comments: 7 pages, 3 tables

title: From Image Interpretation to Clinical Reasoning: Upstream Physician-Context-Aware Multimodal Learning with Causal Reinforcement Learning
text: arXiv:2609.38924 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CV From Image Interpretation to Clinical Reasoning: Upstream Physician-Context-Aware Multimodal Learning with Causal Reinforcement Learning Authors: Jialu Pi , Yanan Ma , Weijie Chen , Owen Crystal , Shubham Trivedi , Stephen Xie , Anna Silverman , Matthew Stib , Chadi Ayoub , Reza Arsanjani , Imon Banerjee Abstract : …complementary patient context, existing medical vision-language models are primarily optimized for radiology interpretation rather than prognostic reasoning. We propose a causal reinforcement learning framework for multimodal clinical reasoning that integrates CXRs and physician-… ▽ More Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) remain the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Opportunistic screening using routinely acquired clinical data offers a scalable approach for identifying high-risk individuals before acute events occur. Although chest X-rays (CXRs) capture latent cardiovascular biomarkers and clinical histories provide complementary patient context, existing medical vision-language models are primarily optimized for radiology interpretation rather than prognostic reasoning. We propose a causal reinforcement learning framework for multimodal clinical reasoning that integrates CXRs and physician- authored clinical histories for opportunistic MACE prediction. The framework introduces (1) a role-decoupled dual-LLM architecture that separates reasoning from risk prediction, (2) a dual-action causal reinforcement learning policy for evidence selection and reasoning optimization, and (3) causal token pruning to learn compact multimodal representations. Evaluated on an internal cohort, an emergency department cohort, and the external MIMIC dataset, the proposed framework consistently outperformed unimodal baselines and state-of-the-art medical vision-language models, achieving AUROCs of 0.720, 0.760, and 0.845, respectively. It also substantially improved reasoning quality, achieving higher GREEN scores and higher expert preference while maintaining robust predictive performance across diverse patient populations. △ Less Submitted 30 September, 2026; originally announced September 2026.

title: Authority Bias in Language Models: Source Deference and User Agreement Are Not Interchangeable
text: arXiv:2609.37616 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.LG cs.CL Authority Bias in Language Models: Source Deference and User Agreement Are Not Interchangeable Authors: Abhinav Rajeev Kumar , Paras Chopra Abstract : …with how authoritative the note sounds. Source deference and user agreement are not behaviorally interchangeable inside the model: on matched items with the same wrong answer, causal interventions can selectively suppress one without equally affecting the other. In three open-weight families, removing a fitted source direction lowers source compliance by 65-… ▽ More Language models tend to agree with whatever a user asserts, and post-training increasingly targets this sycophancy so that models evaluate claims on their merits rather than deferring to the user. Yet the same models are far more compliant when a wrong answer is attributed to a verified source, which is how retrieval results, tool outputs, and grounded-search content often present information. We measure this gap across five open-weight families and three closed APIs. A single verified-source note endorsing a wrong answer flips 45-88% of baseline-correct responses in seven of eight models, and compliance rises with how authoritative the note sounds. Source deference and user agreement are not behaviorally interchangeable inside the model: on matched items with the same wrong answer, causal interventions can selectively suppress one without equally affecting the other. In three open-weight families, removing a fitted source direction lowers source compliance by 65-80 percentage points while removing a user or assistant direction has far smaller effects, and removing the user direction shows the reverse preference. A separately fitted intervention derived from source-versus-user cue activations moves compliance in both directions while leaving the prompt text unchanged. An authority direction fitted on trivia also transfers to PIQA and multi-turn SYCON dialogues without refitting, and removing it lowers wrong-source compliance by tens of percentage points in four of five families with no detected change in MMLU-Pro or GSM8K accuracy at our evaluation sizes. Source deference and user agreement therefore need separate evaluation. △ Less Submitted 29 September, 2026; originally announced September 2026. Comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Main Conference, Poster). 33 pages, 8 figures. Project page: https://authority-bias.vercel.app/ . Code: https://github.com/Lossfunk/authority-bias

title: Evidence Over Ideology: A Quantitative Assessment of LTNs and Blanket 20 mph Regimes in London
text:
arXiv:2609.37266 [ pdf , ps , other ] stat.OT Evidence Over Ideology: A Quantitative Assessment of LTNs and Blanket 20 mph Regimes in London Authors: Stylianos Kampakis Abstract : …via sign-only orders without physical traffic calming, this work evaluates the blanket statutory model rather than lower urban speeds in principle.
  For LTNs, we apply a causal pipeline combining naive pre/post comparisons, Empirical Bayes shrinkage for Regression to the Mean (RTM), and spatial Difference-in-Differences. Naive comparisons suggest substantia… ▽ More We evaluate the road safety implications of Low Traffic Neighbourhoods (LTNs) and blanket 20 mph speed limits in London using injury-collision records (2020-2024). Because London implemented 20 mph limits primarily via sign-only orders without physical traffic calming, this work evaluates the blanket statutory model rather than lower urban speeds in principle.
  For LTNs, we apply a causal pipeline combining naive pre/post comparisons, Empirical Bayes shrinkage for Regression to the Mean (RTM), and spatial Difference-in-Differences. Naive comparisons suggest substantial crash reductions, but Empirical Bayes adjustment reveals much of this reflects mean reversion. After correction, only one zone exhibits a statistically significant inside-area reduction. We find no consistent evidence of boundary-road crash displacement nor uniform inside safety gains. Given the modest corrected benefits, small journey-time increases on boundary roads (approximately 10 seconds per vehicle) monetarily negate safety gains.
  For 20 mph versus 30 mph roads, five associational methods across 14 contexts show that the aggregate difference in the fatal or serious (KSI) collision share is negligible (0.6 percentage points). Controlling the false discovery rate, four contexts display robustly higher KSI shares on 20 mph roads: A-roads, junctions, pedestrian crossings, and single carriageways, with no context showing a robust reduction. In movement corridors where road geometry cues higher speeds, sign-only limits fail to self-enforce.
  These findings highlight a structural "wrong-road problem." Indiscriminate sign-only limits impose economic drag without proportionate safety returns. Transport authorities should move away from blanket statutory defaults and return to targeted physical engineering on high-harm corridors. △ Less Submitted 29 September, 2026; originally announced September 2026.

title: Measurement-Error-Aware Causal Distributed-Lag Quantile Modeling of Indoor Air Pollution and Short-Term Lung-Function Deterioration
text: arXiv:2609.31646 [ pdf , ps , other ] stat.AP cs.AI cs.CY cs.LG Measurement-Error-Aware Causal Distributed-Lag Quantile Modeling of Indoor Air Pollution and Short-Term Lung-Function Deterioration Authors: Shayma Alkobaisi , Anas Ali Abstract : …delayed exposure effects, time-varying confounding, and heterogeneous lower-tail responses limit risk estimation. We present CAUSALQUANT-ASTHMA, a measurement-error-aware causal quantile distributed-lag framework for short-horizon peak expiratory flow analysis. Sparse reference measurements train a nonlinear calibration model; stabilized sequential generali… ▽ More Low-cost indoor air-quality sensors could support personalized asthma prevention, but their nonlinear measurement error, delayed exposure effects, time-varying confounding, and heterogeneous lower-tail responses limit risk estimation. We present CAUSALQUANT-ASTHMA, a measurement-error-aware causal quantile distributed-lag framework for short-horizon peak expiratory flow analysis. Sparse reference measurements train a nonlinear calibration model; stabilized sequential generalized-propensity weights address measured exposure assignment; and a susceptibility-modulated, smooth, noncrossing quantile model estimates lag-specific and sustained-exposure contrasts. Because no authorized cohort simultaneously provided dense indoor sensing, reference co-location, and outcome-compatible longitudinal data, evaluation used five semi-synthetic panels with known counterfactual truth, 150 patients and 12,600 patient-days per realization. Across eight methods, CAUSALQUANT achieved a dose-response integrated absolute error of 0.304 plus or minus 0.094, improving 24.2 percent over the strongest measurement-error and propensity-weighted baseline. It also obtained the lowest overall pinball loss, 1.065, while maintaining zero quantile crossings and 78.1 percent coverage for the nominal 80 percent interval. Sensor calibration reduced held-out exposure RMSE by 33.7 percent. Stress tests quantified degradation under sensor noise, missing personal measurements, and hidden confounding. These findings establish methodological feasibility and reproducibility, not clinical effectiveness; prospective, governance-approved external validation is required before patient-level interpretation or deployment. △ Less Submitted 12 September, 2026; originally announced September 2026.

title: From Spectrum Regulation to Computational Enforcement: An Auditable Governance Architecture for Adaptive Spectrum Sharing
text: arXiv:2609.29571 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CR cs.IT cs.NI eess.SP From Spectrum Regulation to Computational Enforcement: An Auditable Governance Architecture for Adaptive Spectrum Sharing Authors: Navaneetha Krishnan Kamalakannan , Harinisri Velmurugan Abstract : Spectrum governance requires rules to be translated into machine-executable decisions while preserving incumbent protection, regulatory authority , and an auditable record of why a decision was made. We present SPECTRA-GOV, a Tri-Layer Adaptive Governance Architecture (TLAGA) connecting international treaty coordination, national adaptive licensing, and real-… ▽ More Spectrum governance requires rules to be translated into machine-executable decisions while preserving incumbent protection, regulatory authority , and an auditable record of why a decision was made. We present SPECTRA-GOV, a Tri-Layer Adaptive Governance Architecture (TLAGA) connecting international treaty coordination, national adaptive licensing, and real-time enforcement. The work builds on the original reference implementation preserved at v0.1.0-paper and adds a post-audit evaluation layer rather than replacing it. V2 introduces controlled spectral-contention scenarios, corrected geodesic-distance calculation, per-operator selective authorization , paired baseline counterfactuals, policy perturbation, regulatory-change analysis, and causal provenance. Across 10,000 scenarios in each of seven contention classes, incumbent protection was 100.00% in the no-contention control, 99.92-99.87% in weak-to-dynamic classes, 99.47% under strong overlap, and 90.00% in the adversarial close-proximity class. In a paired S3 baseline experiment, selective authorization achieved 100% incumbent protection and 89.43% access opportunity, while the population-wide dynamic baseline achieved 99.91% protection and 99.53% access. Identical results for the dynamic-SAS and SPECTRA-GOV selective variants mean selective admission alone is not claimed as an exclusive algorithmic novelty. The contribution is the integration of policy representation, computational enforcement, auditability, provenance. Enforcement timing was measured in-process, with mean latency increasing from 0.028 ms for one operator to 1.682 ms for 500 operators; these are software benchmarks, not field measurements. The results establish a reproducible computational governance prototype and identify remaining questions before operational or regulatory claims can be made. △ Less Submitted 30 August, 2026; originally announced September 2026. Comments: 43 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to Telecommunication Policy. Code: https://github.com/ka-cyber/spectra-gov

title: Forced Yet Free: What Magicians' Forcing Reveals Beyond Intentional Binding
text: arXiv:2609.27416 [ pdf ] cs.HC Forced Yet Free: What Magicians' Forcing Reveals Beyond Intentional Binding Authors: Koichi Toida Abstract : …the processes by which feeling of agency and judgment of agency are constructed. On this basis, a distinction is drawn between intentional binding, which concerns the temporal/ causal relation between action and outcome, and the different binding problem exposed by forcing: the relation between a choice and its author .… ▽ More In magicians' forcing, spectators may experience a choice as self-determined even when that choice has been externally directed. Research on the sense of agency has developed largely around action-outcome relations, most notably intentional binding; however, the problem of choice authorship (why a particular choice is experienced as originating from oneself) must be treated as distinct. This paper integrates research on agency and forcing by distinguishing the locus of intervention within the choice-action-outcome chain, self-attribution at the Decision, Action, and Outcome levels, and the processes by which feeling of agency and judgment of agency are constructed. On this basis, a distinction is drawn between intentional binding, which concerns the temporal/ causal relation between action and outcome, and the different binding problem exposed by forcing: the relation between a choice and its author . This theoretical relation is termed authorship binding. Authorship binding does not denote a new implicit measure; rather, it refers to the constructive relation through which a choice whose formation has been directed by external factors can nevertheless be experienced as originating from the self. Forcing can sustain this relation not by eliminating agency, but by selectively preserving, substituting, and redistributing agency cues. XR, in which body-centred spatial relations can be manipulated, is further conceptualised as a medium for extending the forced-yet-free structure into space. △ Less Submitted 12 October, 2026; v1 submitted 23 September, 2026; originally announced September 2026. Comments: 9 pages, 1 figure. v2: Minor theoretical clarification and an additional reference

title: Strategic Classification Has a Missing Lever: Audit Risk
text: arXiv:2609.22534 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.GT cs.HC cs.LG Strategic Classification Has a Missing Lever: Audit Risk Authors: Raman Ebrahimi , Massimo Franceschetti Abstract : …fake can only be down-weighted or discarded. However, in many settings the decision maker can also verify: lenders verify income, admissions offices check documents, and tax authorities audit returns. In this paper, we propose a model of strategic classification in which the firm jointly designs a linear classifier and an \emph{audit profile}, which assigns… ▽ More Strategic classification studies how a decision maker should choose a classifier when the agents being classified can adjust their features in response to it. In existing models, the classifier is the only instrument available to the decision maker, and therefore a feature that is predictive but easy to fake can only be down-weighted or discarded. However, in many settings the decision maker can also verify: lenders verify income, admissions offices check documents, and tax authorities audit returns. In this paper, we propose a model of strategic classification in which the firm jointly designs a linear classifier and an \emph{audit profile}, which assigns to each fakeable feature a probability of detection and a penalty when caught. We show that under linear costs, the classifier affects the audit problem only through the distribution of gaming rents it induces, so that the joint design problem decomposes into the choice of a score rule and an audit allocation problem. We use this decomposition to characterize the optimal audit allocation, to identify when the allocation problem is tractable and when it is NP-hard (namely, when agents can game through overlapping features under an inspection cap), and to bound the regret of a firm that has to learn the rents by auditing. We further show that audit intensity is a quantity to be tuned rather than maximized: welfare is single-peaked in it, and a firm and a social planner disagree on the mix of detection and penalty that delivers a given level of deterrence. Notably, two populations with identical costs and causal structure can game in one domain and improve in the other, a difference that a cost-only model cannot account for. Together, our findings highlight that whether a feature is ``gameable'' depends on the institution's verification policy as much as on the feature itself. △ Less Submitted 18 September, 2026; originally announced September 2026.

title: Three-dimensional vector waves in time-variant materials, with applications in time-reversed focusing and Green's function retrieval
text: arXiv:2609.20357 [ pdf , ps , other ] physics.app-ph Three-dimensional vector waves in time-variant materials, with applications in time-reversed focusing and Green's function retrieval Authors: Kees Wapenaar , Dirk-Jan van Manen Abstract : The behavior of wave propagation and scattering in time-variant materials has been studied by many authors , for electromagnetic as well as for mechanical waves. Most studies consider two-dimensional waves, governed by scalar wave equations. Here we introduce a unified wave equation for three-dimensional electromagnetic and elastodynamic vector-wave propagati… ▽ More The behavior of wave propagation and scattering in time-variant materials has been studied by many authors , for electromagnetic as well as for mechanical waves.
